methodological_rigor.justification: Solid preclinical design with appropriate controls including OATP inhibitor studies and temperature controls. In vivo experiments conducted in replicate (n=5 K1, n=10 8505C) with H&E histological validation. Appropriate statistical tests employed (ANOVA, Friedman, paired t-test). However, lacks formal randomization procedures, blinding not mentioned, and no pre-specification of endpoints as would be expected for rigorous preclinical work.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical animal study targeting clinically relevant problem of intraoperative detection of microscopic positive surgical margins in thyroid cancer. Clear translational pathway articulated for both conventional and robotic thyroidectomy. However, entirely preclinical; authors explicitly state additional validation needed for human relevance and acknowledge limitations in cell line models.

reporting_quality.justification: Study adequately describes materials and methods but falls short of full ARRIVE compliance. Missing key elements: no explicit statement of randomization procedure for animal allocation, blinding not reported, no pre-specification of outcomes or analysis plan. Protocol approval documented but incomplete. No data or code availability mentioned.

novelty_literature.justification: pH-sensitive probes for tumor margin detection already demonstrated in liver, colon, and ovarian cancers (as cited in text). Application to thyroid cancer is incremental extension of established approach rather than novel mechanism or first-in-class application. Authors acknowledge previous work with these probes in human thyroid cancer models.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear introduction, comprehensive methods section, logical results presentation with effective figures comparing fluorescence imaging and histology. Tables provide quantitative data clearly. Some sections could be more concise but overall publication-ready quality with good flow and minimal grammatical issues.

key_strengths: Addresses clinically relevant problem of microscopic positive margin detection with clear application to both conventional and robotic thyroidectomy
Rigorous in vivo validation with dual tumor models (papillary and anaplastic) and H&E histology correlation confirming imaging findings
Well-controlled cellular studies demonstrating OATP-mediated uptake mechanism with appropriate transporter inhibition and temperature controls
key_concerns: Entirely preclinical with acknowledged need for human validation before clinical translation
Incremental novelty—pH-sensitive probes already demonstrated for margin detection in multiple other cancer types
Limited discussion of practical considerations: probe manufacturing complexity, clinical feasibility, cost, and regulatory pathway not addressed
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent preclinical work soundly executed but limited by incremental novelty and purely exploratory status. Best suited for tier 4 venue given narrow scope and full preclinical stage.
